title: Isandro and the Wolf
premise: Beatrix Winterbourne, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has survived twenty years in Vellamark by keeping her magic small and her head down. When a stranger named Isandro arrives carrying a prophecy book written a century before her birth — with tonight's date inked on its final page — she learns the country they stand in was erased from existence a hundred years ago, and everyone in it is living inside a memory that is finally expiring. To escape, they must find the Door of Unmaking at the heart of the vanished kingdom, pursued by the Custodians who feed the erasure with stolen memories. Beatrix must choose between preserving her own past and spending it to open the door; Isandro, revealed as the last true citizen of Vellamark, chooses erasure so she can walk out carrying its memory. The book ends with Beatrix outside, alone but not empty, carving the dead country's story into bone so it can never be forgotten again.
about_author: Marguerite Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of families displaced by border changes, an experience that haunts everything she writes. She lives near the sea with two indifferent cats and a growing collection of antique maps of places that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In her market stall, Beatrix sells a luck-charm to a nervous stranger, Isandro, and hears her dead mother's voice warn her about him for the first time in years. That night she finds his purchase recorded in a century-old prophecy book bearing tomorrow's date. Emotional beat: dread disguised as ordinary life, the first crack in twenty years of careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Isandro returns, unafraid, claiming he was sent by the book itself. Reading from it, Beatrix discovers Vellamark — the name of her city's country — appears nowhere else in any record, yet every bone she touches hums with grief for it. Custodians arrive at her door asking questions about 'unregistered memory.' Emotional beat: vertigo as her whole world reveals itself as a forgery.

chapters.title: A Country With No Borders
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Fleeing through the night market, Isandro explains: Vellamark was erased a century ago, its people folded into neighboring nations, and the prophecy book is the only surviving map of what was lost. He is searching for the Door of Unmaking. Beatrix refuses to believe him until a Custodian's touch strips a childhood memory from her mind. Emotional beat: denial curdling into fury.

chapters.title: The Custodians' Tithe
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. They learn the Custodians sustain the erasure by harvesting memories from those who still unknowingly carry Vellamark inside them — including Beatrix. Her grandmother's lullaby surfaces half-eaten, wrong. A dying archivist gives them the first clue to the Door: it opens only where the oldest bones lie. Emotional beat: grief made physical, the theft of the past.

chapters.title: The Ossuary Road
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Traveling toward the old capital's catacombs, they shelter with a village whose elders speak Vellamarkish in their sleep without knowing why. Isandro grows strangely fluent among them, and Beatrix realizes he belongs here in a way no outsider could. He deflects. Custodian riders burn the village's dream-records behind them. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Isandro's Name in the Book
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In a ruined chapel, Beatrix finds Isandro's own name written in the prophecy book — dated one hundred years ago. Confronted, he confesses: he is the last child born a citizen of Vellamark, kept outside the erasure as a living key to the Door. She realizes their meeting was engineered by the book, not chance. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with compassion.

chapters.title: The Price of the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Reaching the catacombs beneath the drowned capital, they find the Door sealed and learn its cost: it opens only when someone willingly surrenders all memory of Vellamark to feed the erasure's hunger — or when the last citizen gives himself back to it entirely. Custodians close in. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of survival, love measured against oblivion.

chapters.title: Everything We Were
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Trapped in the ossuary, Beatrix does the unthinkable: she begins giving up her own memories of Vellamark — her grandmother, her mother's voice, twenty years of small charms — to pry the Door ajar. Each memory spent is rendered in bone as she carves it, refusing to let the Custodians be the only keepers. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship, loss transformed into record.

chapters.title: The Last Citizen
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the threshold, with the Door straining open, Isandro understands the erasure will simply reseal unless its anchor returns. He steps back into Vellamark's fading memory-land, becoming the country's final inhabitant, and presses the prophecy book into Beatrix's hands. Their goodbye happens inside a single shared remembered evening. Emotional beat: climax — chosen erasure as the ultimate act of witness.

chapters.title: Carved in Bone
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Outside, in a nation that never heard of Vellamark, Beatrix opens a new stall selling not charms but carvings: the names, streets, and songs of a country only she remembers, each piece humming faintly to those who carry its blood. The book's final page now reads blank except for one line — 'and she told them.' Emotional beat: mourning transfigured into memory-keeping; justice outside any law.
